tochigi-sports-flow.title: Tochigi Prefecture Sports Commission: prefecture-wide travel from mobility data
tochigi-sports-flow.eyebrow: xBUILD / Mobility analytics & digital twin / Sports & regions
tochigi-sports-flow.lead: YELLOW has joined the Tochigi Prefecture Sports Commission's programme to promote prefecture-wide travel using mobility data (October 2026). We analyse and visualise the demographics and routes of fans attending home games of the Utsunomiya Brex, Tochigi SC and Tochigi Honda Heat, and feed the findings into measures that turn match days into trips around the prefecture.
alts: Tochigi tourism intelligence | Prefecture-wide digital twin: attractions and transport
Brex Arena Utsunomiya digital twin | Inside the arena on an Utsunomiya Brex home game
Green Stadium digital twin | Site footfall and OD analysis on a Tochigi Honda Heat home game
Kanseki Stadium Tochigi digital twin | Site footfall on a Tochigi SC home game
Tochigi tourism intelligence | Regional access routes and model itineraries

paras: Professional sport generates more than a match: eating, shopping and sightseeing around the venue. To design measures that spread that activity across a region, you first need to know where spectators go before and after the game and how they move.

In this programme we use mobility data to analyse and visualise the demographics and routes of fans attending home games of the prefecture's professional teams. The findings feed into measures that connect match days with local retail and tourism, aiming to increase travel within the prefecture, the exchange population and regional economic activity.

items: Analysis of spectator demographics (gender, age band, estimated home area) and movement patterns from mobility data
Visualisation of spectator routes and behaviour within the region
Evidence-based design of measures to promote travel within the prefecture
Exploring links between match attendance and local retail and tourism assets

A prefecture-wide digital twin built from real terrain, transport and attraction data, with visitor counts, overnight stays, spend and catchment areas analysed in one place, and progress against strategic KPIs tracked on a single screen

paras: Travel-promotion planning by local governments and sports commissions, linking home games with local retail and tourism, and a shared data platform for government, teams and businesses.

spec: Tochigi Prefecture Sports Commission / home games of the Utsunomiya Brex, Tochigi SC and Tochigi Honda Heat
Location data collected with user consent and statistically processed (no personally identifiable information), public statistics, GSI terrain and transport data
Spectator demographics, catchment, routes, visitor counts, overnight stays, spend, strategic KPIs
Prefecture-wide digital twin, site footfall and OD analysis around the stadiums, seat mapping inside the arena, KPI dashboard
Understanding spectator behaviour on match days and designing travel-promotion measures (matches and timing to be agreed with the parties involved)
Mobility-data analysis and visualisation, support for designing measures

soip-iwaki-fc.title: Japan Sports Agency SOIP × Iwaki FC: mobility analysis for stadium access and a new-stadium concept
soip-iwaki-fc.lead: Under the Japan Sports Agency's Sports Open Innovation Platform (SOIP), we worked with Iwaki FC and LocationMind Inc. on mobility analysis: easing car-park congestion on match days, analysing movement inside the stadium, and assessing location and access including the move to a new stadium.
alts: Key visual of the SPORTS OPEN INNOVATION BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT 2025 CONFERENCE (18 December 2025, Tokyo)

paras: SOIP is a programme run by the Japan Sports Agency to create new businesses and regional value through co-creation between sports organisations and companies. This project was selected to use mobility-data analysis for better access and regional problem-solving around Iwaki FC's new-stadium concept.

Where home-game visitors come from, how they travel, which routes they take and how they move inside the venue are essential inputs for improving car parks and circulation, and for assessing the site of a new stadium. At the CONFERENCE in Tokyo on 18 December 2025 we gave an interim report together with our partners.

items: Easing car-park congestion: analysing arrival times, routes and car-park use to design dispersal and guidance measures
Movement inside the stadium: visualising circulation and dwell to pinpoint crowded spots and improvements
Analysis including the move to a new stadium: comparing location and access from catchment, modes of transport and spill-over to nearby facilities
Turning the findings into material for measures that the club, local government and transport operators can share

paras: Match-day operations at sports clubs, transport and parking plans with local governments and operators, and location and access studies for new stadiums and large venues.

spec: Visitors to Iwaki FC home games, the stadium surroundings and interior
Beacon and GPS location data (collected with user consent and statistically processed; no personally identifiable information), surveys and ticket data
Visitor demographics, catchment, mode of access, routes, car-park use, movement and dwell inside the venue
Easing car-park congestion, improving circulation inside the stadium, and assessing location and access including a move to a new stadium
Mobility-data analysis, visualisation and support for planning measures (a Japan Sports Agency SOIP project, with Iwaki FC and LocationMind)

factory-digital-twin.title: Factory digital twin: tracking people, simulating productivity and relocation
factory-digital-twin.lead: A multi-building manufacturing plant rebuilt as a BIM-based 3D model from the site down to the building interiors. Worker location logs are overlaid to track movement, travel between processes is quantified to study productivity, and the relocation of processes and equipment is simulated across the whole site.
alts: Overview of the BIM model of a factory interior: columns, beams and roof trusses, equipment, pipes and ducts, logistics routes
The factory interior from a worker's eye level: aisles, pipe racks, tanks and equipment labels
Operation replay inside the factory: a forklift on the aisle and product storage
Overview of the whole building with operation replay and congestion display showing workers and vehicles
3D model of the whole site: buildings, tanks, internal roads and vehicles
Relocation simulation: the buildings on site and candidate locations for relocated processes

paras: At a manufacturing plant with several buildings, the time spent moving and transporting between processes was shaping productivity. How people and vehicles actually moved inside the plant, however, was known only from drawings and intuition.

We rebuilt the site and the building interiors in 3D, overlaid measured location data to show what is happening now, and built an environment where improvement and relocation plans can be compared on the same model. The plant and the company are not named.

items: 3D and BIM of the interior: columns, beams and roof trusses, equipment, pipes and ducts, logistics routes and process zones modelled part by part. Viewable in overview, section and worker's-eye views, and usable for clash checks and maintenance-clearance studies

Tracking people: worker location logs from beacons and similar sources replayed in 3D by day and by process. Routes, dwell and congestion are visualised to pinpoint issues in circulation and transport

Productivity simulation: the number, distance and time of movements between processes are quantified in staff-hours, and the savings from changes to layout or staffing are estimated. Comparison against a baseline and automatic optimisation candidates are supported

Relocation simulation: plans to move processes or equipment to another building are studied on the 3D model of the whole site, comparing travel distance and time and the staff required. Layouts can be saved and exported for stakeholders

paras: Layout and circulation improvements, studies ahead of equipment renewal or process relocation, planning of new plants and moves, and investment decisions made by the shop floor and management looking at the same 3D model.

spec: A manufacturing plant: the whole site and the interiors of several buildings
Building drawings and equipment specifications, site visits, worker location logs (beacons etc.), process and staffing data
Movements between processes (count, distance, time), staff-hours, congestion and dwell, transport distance
BIM display, equipment sections, worker's-eye view, operation replay, congestion display, routes, productivity analysis, relocation comparison, saving and export of layouts
Circulation and transport improvements, staffing studies, relocation of processes and equipment, new-plant planning
Construction of 3D and BIM models, location-data analysis, and development of a browser-based planning tool
